who: Peng Duanshu · On Learning, 18th century, tr. from Chinese
quote: Are the things of the world hard or easy? Do them, and even the hard become easy. Do not do them, and even the easy become hard.
meaning: Hard or easy is up to you. Do it, and hard turns easy. Don't, and easy turns hard.

quote: At first... you really have to focus and concentrate, you're kind of slow... And you get better at it as time goes on... And then it becomes liberating, because you don't have to think about it, you just do it.
meaning: A new skill is slow at first and takes all your focus. Keep practising, and soon you just do it.

who: Goethe · Maxims and Reflections, tr. T. Bailey Saunders, 1893
quote: To see a difficult thing lightly handled gives us the impression of the impossible.
meaning: Easy-looking skill is just a lot of practice.

who: B. K. S. Iyengar · Light on Yoga, 1966
quote: When one has mastered an āsana, it comes with effortless ease and causes no discomfort. The bodily movements become graceful.
meaning: Once your body truly learns an asana, it feels easy, comfortable and graceful.

who: Aristotle · Rhetoric I.11, tr. John Henry Freese, 1926
quote: Application, study, and intense effort are also painful, for these involve necessity and compulsion, if they have not become habitual; for then habit makes them pleasant.
meaning: Hard work feels painful while it is new. Once it becomes a habit, the habit makes it pleasant.

who: Leo Tolstoy · Anna Karenina, tr. Constance Garnett, 1901
quote: ...it seemed not his hands that swung the scythe, but the scythe mowing of itself... These were the most blissful moments.
meaning: After long practice, the work seemed to do itself. Those were his happiest moments.

quote: The boy at the temple gate chants the sutra he was never taught.
meaning: Hear and see it every day, and one day you can do it without lessons. That is a Mysore room.

who: Ouyang Xiu · The Oil Seller, about 1067, tr. from Chinese
quote: ...slowly ladled oil, letting it drip in through the coin's hole without wetting the coin. Then he said: 'I have no secret either. My hands are simply practised.'
meaning: There is no magic secret. Hands that do something again and again get good at it.

who: Ralph Waldo Emerson · The Conduct of Life, 1860
quote: A humorous friend of mine thinks, that the reason why Nature is so perfect in her art, and gets up such inconceivably fine sunsets, is, that she has learned how, at last, by dint of doing the same thing so very often.
meaning: Even nature's sunsets are so good because she has done them so very often.

who: Krishna · Bhagavad Gita 6.23-25, tr. Edwin Arnold, 1885
quote: Steadfastly the will / Must toil thereto, till efforts end in ease... so, step by step, it comes / To gift of peace assured and heart assuaged.
meaning: Step by step, hard effort turns into ease.
